title: The Lord's Day kept
hookLine: Scottish Presbyterians kept a quiet, holy Sunday

lines: AN UPPER ROOM, THE FIRST DAY.
A YOUNG MAN IN THE WINDOW.
cards: It's the first day of the week, in Troas, and the church has gathered in an upstairs room to break bread. Paul is leaving in the morning, so he talks until midnight.
A young man named Eutychus, sitting in the window, sinks into a deep sleep, falls from the third loft, and is taken up dead. Paul goes down, embraces him, and says his life is in him.
Then he goes back upstairs, breaks bread, and talks until daybreak. A glimpse, from Acts, of Christians gathering on the first day.

teach.h: THE FIRST DAY OF THE WEEK.
teach.b: The Gospels say the empty tomb was found on the first day of the week. Christians came to gather on that day, and in Revelation, John writes, "I was in the Spirit on the Lord's day."
Scottish Presbyterians, heirs of the Reformed way this week has followed, kept all of it.

Their Westminster Confession calls it the Christian Sabbath: rest from ordinary work and from recreations, the whole day given to worship, in church and at home, with room for works of necessity and mercy.
In homes that kept it this way, the Sunday clothes came out, in some the meal was made the day before, and the hours went to church, the Bible, the catechism, a quiet walk, a visit to someone ill.
From outside it could look stern. To those who loved it, it was a day the rest of the week couldn't touch.
Behind it sits the old commandment, "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy," and Isaiah's picture of people who "call the sabbath a delight." Christians keep the day in different ways.
Seventh-day Adventists keep Saturday, the seventh day, as the Sabbath. Others hold that in Christ every day belongs to God, and keep Sunday for worship without the full Sabbath rules.
Jesus himself said, "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath." Jewish neighbors keep their own Sabbath on the seventh day.
This week walked through common prayer, Luther's garland for his barber, an only comfort, psalms in rhyme, a long meditation, a family at the table. It ends with a whole day handed back.

how: Christians gather for worship on Sunday, the Lord's Day. In the Scottish Presbyterian tradition the whole day was kept for church, Bible reading, rest and works of mercy; Seventh-day Adventists keep Saturday as the Sabbath.

games.q: what does “the lord's day kept” mean?
o: a holiday marking the day Jesus was born
a Sunday spent strictly in church from dawn to dusk
Sunday set apart whole for worship, rest and mercy

it left room for works of necessity and mercy.
Jesus said the sabbath was made for man

every church keeps the Lord's day the same way

games.q: you're Paul. it's past midnight, you've talked all evening, and a young man has just fallen from the window. what do you do?
o: end the gathering and send everyone home.
go down, embrace him, then go back up and break bread.
keep talking; someone else will see to him.
games.why: he goes down, embraces him, says his life is in him, then breaks bread and talks until daybreak. Acts says they brought the young man alive.

practice: Keep a small sabbath right now: phone face down, out of reach if you can, shoulders dropped. For these minutes nothing needs answering, fixing or finishing, and any task that floats up can wait; it will still be there.
If you pray, give these minutes to God; if you don't, simply rest in them.

wordCard.voice: The Lord's Day kept. Sunday, the first day of the week, set apart whole for rest, worship and mercy, the way Scottish Presbyterians kept it.

orig.note: Greek, Revelation 1:10: the Lord's day, the day belonging to the Lord.

carryVoice: Your line: a day set apart. A whole week, ending in a whole day. Until tomorrow.
